conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: SAME clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.3 "SORT and SORT-MERGE are equivalent" -> OK SR1. The grammar takes SORT | SORT_MERGE as one alternative slot and nothing downstream distinguishes them (BindIoControl treats both as the storage-economy no-op arm, and no rule anywhere reads SORT() vs SORT_MERGE()). Probes: gr4_sortarea (`SAME SORT AREA FOR S1 F3` + SORT S1 USING F1 GIVING F2 -> AAAAAA, CCCCCC) and sr1_sortmerge (`SAME SORT-MERGE AREA FOR S1 F3`, same program -> AAAAAA) behave identically (F3 is kept out of the SORT statement so the probe respects SORT §14.9.40.3 SR10). Equivalence holds structurally; note the equivalence is currently trivial because neither spelling feeds the (unimplemented) SR5/SR6/SR8/SR10 checks - when those land they must treat both spellings as the sort-merge-area format. No spec-derived test. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME clause is base I-O-CONTROL language in every edition; no Annex E change entry names it)]

rows.subject: SAME clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.3 "The files specified in a given SAME clause need not all have the same organization or access" -> OK SR4 (a permission). BindIoControl links files by their record anchors with no organization/access test, and nothing else screens it. Probe gr2_mixed: `SAME RECORD AREA FOR F1 F2 F3` over ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL (PIC X(4)), RELATIVE ACCESS SEQUENTIAL (group X(2)+X(6)) and LINE SEQUENTIAL (PIC X(10)) compiles at 2023 and runs correctly (see GR-12.4.6.4.4-2); fmt_all_ok mixes SD and FD files in one clause. No spec-derived test mixes organizations. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME clause is base I-O-CONTROL language in every edition; no Annex E change entry names it)]
rows.rule-text: The files specified in a given SAME clause need not all have the same organization or access.

rows.subject: SAME clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "No more than one of these files may be in the open mode at a given time" -> OK GR1. Two halves: (a) the files 'are to use the same memory area' - a storage-ECONOMY permission with no program-observable content for a conforming program: only one member is ever open, and a closed file's record area is unavailable (§14.9.6.4 GR7) so a program cannot observe whether the areas coincide; Annex D (informative) describes it as saving memory space. BindIoControl binds Format 1 as a deliberate no-op (doc comment: 'storage-economy permissions ... bound as conformant no-ops'). (b) the open-mode restriction is a constraint on the PROGRAM with no exception condition or runtime check specified (grep of the spec finds no EC or OPEN rule keyed on SAME AREA), so violating it is outside a conforming program. Probe gr1_filearea (`SAME AREA FOR F1 F2`, write/close F1, write/close F2, read each back) -> F1=AAAAAA, F2=BBBBBB, correct at 2023. No spec-derived test. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME clause is base I-O-CONTROL language in every edition; no Annex E change entry names it)]
rows.rule-text: A file-area format SAME clause specifies that two or more files referenced by file-name-1, file-name-2 are to use the same memory area during processing. The area being shared includes all storage areas assigned to the files referenced by file-name-1, file-name-2. No more than one of these files may be in the open mode at a given time.

rows.subject: SAME clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "The extent of such allocation shall be specified by the implementor" -> OK GR4 b). GR4 a)/b) are storage-reuse PERMISSIONS (sort work storage 'is available for reuse'; non-sort file areas 'may be allocated as needed'), c) says non-sort files' areas do NOT share with each other. BindIoControl binds Format 3 as a no-op: nothing is shared or reused, which satisfies a) and b) (permissions not exercised; the b) extent is zero) and c) (every file keeps its own area). Annex A.1 item 169 (extent of allocation) is 'required' but its procedure 'does not have to be documented in the implementor's user documentation', so no CONFORMANCE.md row is owed by this rule. Probe gr4_sortarea (`SAME SORT AREA FOR S1 F3`, SORT S1 USING F1 GIVING F2) -> AAAAAA then CCCCCC, correct. No spec-derived test. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME clause is base I-O-CONTROL language in every edition; no Annex E change entry names it)]
rows.rule-text: A sort-merge-area format SAME clause specifies that memory is shared as follows: a) Any storage area allocated for the sorting or merging of a sort or merge file specified in a sort-merge-area format SAME clause is available for reuse in sorting or merging any of the other sort or merge files specified in that sort-merge-area format SAME clause. b) Storage areas assigned to files specified in a sort-merge-area format SAME clause that do not represent sort or merge files may be allocated as needed for sorting or merging the sort or merge files named in that sort-merge-area format SAME clause. The extent of such allocation shall be specified by the implementor. c) Storage areas assigned to files specified in a sort-merge-area format SAME clause other than sort or merge files do not share the same storage area with each other.

rows.subject: SAME clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "any non-sort and non-merge files associated with file-names specified in that clause shall not be in the open mode" -> OK GR5. A constraint on the PROGRAM during SORT/MERGE; the standard specifies no exception condition or check for its violation (the SORT/MERGE statements key SAME-clause restrictions only as SYNTAX rules on file-name pairs, §14.9.40.3 SR10 / §14.9.24.3 SR11 (cite.py --find OK), which are other rows). Because the Format 3 clause is bound as a no-op (no storage is actually shared with the sort work area), a program that respects GR5 behaves exactly as specified - probe gr4_sortarea (`SAME SORT AREA FOR S1 F3`, F3 never opened) gets the specified output. No spec-derived test. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME clause is base I-O-CONTROL language in every edition; no Annex E change entry names it)]
rows.rule-text: During the processing of a SORT or MERGE statement that refers to a sort or merge file named in a sort-merge-area format SAME clause, any non-sort and non-merge files associated with file-names specified in that clause shall not be in the open mode.

rows.subject: SELF and SUPER
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (--check 8.4.3.8.4 'both reference the object that was used to invoke the method' -> OK §8.4.3.8.4 1)). SELF renders `this.M()` and SUPER `base.M()` (InvokeForm.Self/Super) on the SAME C# receiver `this`, so both reference the invoking object. Probe probe/self-and-super/PGR3.cob (A.M does INVOKE SELF "N"; C.M does INVOKE SUPER "M"; object of class C) prints C.M / A.M / C.N / B.N at --std 2002: the SUPER-invoked base body's SELF is still the C object. conformance:2002/oo_self covers the SELF half (shared per-instance N) only; the SUPER half is probe-verified, so no single spec-derived test closes both halves - test-ref left empty. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO predefined object references; absent from COBOL-85)]
rows.rule-text: SELF and SUPER both reference the object that was used to invoke the method in which the reference to SELF or SUPER appears.

rows.subject: SELF and SUPER
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (--check 8.4.3.8.4 'ignores all the methods defined in the class containing the invocation' -> OK §8.4.3.8.4 3)). For SUPER, searchRoot = cur.Base and the call renders non-virtual `base.M()`, ignoring the containing class and its subclasses; SUPER in a root class -> COBOLNET0827. oo_super: DOG.SPEAK override INVOKE SUPER "SPEAK" prints ANIMAL then DOG (no recursion). Probe probe/self-and-super/PGR3.cob: C INHERITS B INHERITS A, B has no M; C.M's INVOKE SUPER "M" runs A.M (skips C, finds grandparent), and C.N's SUPER "N" runs B.N not C.N - output C.M/A.M/C.N/B.N as derived. || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref emptied: oo_super pins only the 'ignore the containing class' half; the 'and all the methods defined in any subclass of that class' half and the grandparent skip are probe-verified only — The behaviour conforms. I probed the half nobody had tried. In RSUB.cob, B.X does INVOKE SUPER "M" on a C object while both B and C override M, and it prints A.M. The factory flavor (INVOKE SUPER "FM" from B's factory, run on the C factory) prints A.FM. So base.M() is non-virtual and ignores the subclass overrides, as GR3 requires. The adjudicator's PGR3 never exercised this half: no SUPER there runs from a class that has an overriding subclass. The cited golden oo_super is only two levels deep (DOG over ANIMAL, invoked on a DOG). It cannot tell a non-virtual base call apart from a virtual one, and it has no subclass. Closing the row on it over-claims what it proves. This is the same reasoning the adjudicator used to leave GR1's test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO predefined object references; absent from COBOL-85)]
rows.rule-text: If SUPER is specified for a method invocation, the method resolution is based on the set of methods defined within the runtime class of the object that invoked the object referenced by SELF and ignores all the methods defined in the class containing the invocation and all the methods defined in any subclass of that class. NOTE 2 The invoked method will be one that is defined in a superclass.
